items.title: Atom
items.summary: An atom is an extremely small piece of matter. All normal matter – everything that has mass – is made of atoms.

items.title: Molecule
items.summary: A molecule is the smallest amount of a chemical substance that can exist. If a molecule were split into smaller pieces, it would be a different substance.

items.title: Chemical element
items.summary: A chemical element is a substance that is made up of only one type of atom. Atoms are made up of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

items.title: Periodic table
items.summary: The periodic table is a table that puts all known chemical elements in a specific order. Elements that have similar characteristics are often put near each other.

items.title: Oxygen
items.summary: Oxygen is a chemical element. It has the symbol O and atomic number 8.

items.title: Carbon
items.summary: Carbon is a very important chemical element, with a chemical symbol of C. All known life on Earth needs it to survive. Carbon has atomic mass 12 and atomic number 6.

items.title: Water
items.summary: Water (H2O) is a simple chemical compound made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. It is clear, has no taste or smell, and is almost colorless.

items.title: Gold
items.summary: Gold is a soft, dense, bright yellow metal. It is a chemical element.

items.title: Iron
items.summary: This article is about iron the metal. For the tool called iron, see ironing.

items.title: Salt
items.summary: In chemistry, a salt is any neutral chemical compound made of cations (positive ions) attached to anions (negative ions). The most common example of a salt is sodium chloride, with the chemical formula NaCl - this is the table salt that people use in food.

items.title: Acid
items.summary: An acid is a type of chemical compound. The definition of an acid has changed as people discovered more about chemistry.

items.title: Gravity
items.summary: Gravity, or gravitation is one of the fundamental forces of the universe. It is an attraction, or pull, between any two objects with mass.

items.title: Force
items.summary: In physics, a force is a push or pull or a twist between objects. It is called an interaction because if one object acts on another, its action is matched by a reaction from the other object.

items.title: Energy
items.summary: Energy can mean various things:

items.title: Light
items.summary: Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation. It is natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things easier to see.

items.title: Magnet
items.summary: A magnet is made of magnetic metals such as iron, nickel, or cobalt, and sometimes certain rare earth metals like neodymium. When a magnet goes near one of these magnetic metals or another magnet, and the poles (sides) touching are opposite, it will pull, or attract the other object closer.

items.title: Heat
items.summary: Heat, or thermal energy, is the sum of the kinetic energy of atoms or molecules. In thermodynamics, heat means energy which is moved between two things when one of them has a higher temperature than the other.

items.title: Speed of light
items.summary: The speed of light, in any medium, which is usually denoted by c, is a physical constant important in many areas of physics. It is denoted by "c0" especially in vacuum medium, although the symbol 'c' can be used to refer to that in any medium.

items.title: Mass
items.summary: The mass of an object is a measure of how much of it there is. For example, A mountain has more mass than a rock.

items.title: Matter
items.summary: Matter means objects which have mass even when not moving, which is a form of energy that matter has even when it is not moving.

items.title: Gas
items.summary: A gas is one of the main forms, or states, of matter, like solids, liquids, and plasmas. What makes gases special is that they do not have a fixed shape or a set volume.

items.title: Liquid
items.summary: A liquid is a form of matter. It is settled between solid and gas.

items.title: Solid
items.summary: Solid is one of the four common states of matter. The molecules in solids are closely bound together, so they can only vibrate.

items.title: Nuclear power
items.summary: Nuclear power is the controlled use of nuclear energy. Nuclear energy can be released by nuclear reactions in a machine called a nuclear reactor.

items.title: Pressure
items.summary: Pressure means how much force something is pushing on something else with.

items.title: Temperature
items.summary: Temperature is how hot or cold something is. The human body can feel the difference between something which is hot and something which is cold.

items.title: Combustion
items.summary: Combustion is the process of burning. Combustion is a reaction of a fuel with an oxidant to give out heat.

items.title: Laser
items.summary: A laser is a machine that makes an amplified, single-color source of light. It uses special gases, liquids, or crystals to make the light with only a single color.

items.title: Rainbow
items.summary: A rainbow is an arc of colour in the sky that can be seen when the sun shines through falling rain. The pattern of colours, called a spectrum, starts with red on the outside and changes through orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet on the inside.

items.title: Metal
items.summary: Some chemical elements are called metals. Most elements in the periodic table are metals.
